title: Participant Event Guide – Sunday 26 April 2026 (TCS London Marathon)
claims: The participant event guide is for Sunday 26 April 2026.
The guide lists five assembly areas: Blue, Green, Pink, Red and Yellow.
The guide's table gives an explicit start line for Blue, Pink and Red but leaves the start-line cells for Green and Yellow blank.

The guide table gives Blackheath as a 10-minute walk for Blue and Yellow, Maze Hill as a 10-minute walk for Pink and Greenwich as a 20-minute walk for Red; the Green row leaves the nearest-station cell blank.
Start waves run from about 09:30 to 11:30.
All Start Lines close at 11:30, and participants are not permitted to start after that time.

Participants have free travel to the Start on Southeastern services from London stations, DLR, Elizabeth Line, London Underground, Overground and buses by showing their bib, without tapping in or out.
DLR services on Sunday 26 April start at about 05:30 from Tower Gateway and Lewisham, and about 07:00 from Bank and all other DLR routes.
Thames Clippers run every 20 minutes from central London to Greenwich Pier.
Spectators should not travel to the Start, which is for participants only.
Water Refill Stations are available in the Start and Finish Areas and along the route.
The guide's course map legend includes water, refill station, KM marker, vaseline and toilets.
The guide's course map appears on page 13.
Distance markers and timing clocks are at every mile and every 5K point; the clocks show time since the first wave started.
A blue line indicates the shortest route, and participants should let faster runners use it and move left to walk.
Non-noise-cancelling or bone-conduction headphones are allowed, or one earpiece; runners must be able to hear safety instructions.
Wheeled devices such as handbikes, rollerblades, skateboards, scooters and motorised gear are prohibited.
If dropping out, runners should tell staff at the nearest First Aid Point and can wait for a sweep minibus or use public transport free with their bib; the wait for a sweep minibus may be long.
The official cut-off is eight hours after the last participant starts at 11:30, with The Mall closing at 19:30; the Finish Line then moves to St James's Park until midnight.
Participants finishing after 19:30 must move onto the pavement to complete their marathon.
Tailwalkers and cycle marshals maintain an eight-hour pace, and participants predicting over seven hours start on the Pink Start.
Participants outside the eight-hour pace must be self-sufficient after Drinks Stations close; toilets remain available until midnight.
There is no bag-drop facility in the Green Assembly Area, and only official event kitbags are accepted.
Post-event travel is free until 20:00 on London Underground, Overground, Elizabeth Line, buses and DLR; Southeastern trains do not offer free post-event travel.
Westminster station will be exit-only.
Results are online within 24 hours and photos within 48 hours via Sportograf.
The Meet and Greet Area is up to 30 minutes' walk from the Finish Line, with lettered Meeting Points at Whitehall, Horse Guards Parade and Horse Guards Road.
Vaseline is at Miles 14, 17, 20 and 22.
Toilets are at the Start, every mile from 1 to 24 and at the Finish; accessible toilets are at the Start, Finish, Miles 1 and 2 and every even mile thereafter.
The guide advises runners to pack a food item in their kitbag to eat after finishing.
The guide says participants should complete their medical information on the back of their bib.
The guide says only participate if fit and well and to read the medical advice from event Medical Director Professor Sanjay Sharma.
The guide says to call 999 in an emergency.
